```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use an API client when you need platform features beyond a SQL connection:
find workspaces, read OneLake files, query a semantic model, or list Databricks
warehouses.

Create the API client inside `server()` and pass a fabricQueryR or brickster function to
`$call()`. You use that function's usual arguments and return value; the
client supplies authentication for the signed-in person. The
[getting-started guide](getting-started.html) shows how to create `auth`.

## Fabric functions

Install `fabricQueryR`. Configure `oauth_db_microsoft_client()` with the
services your app needs:

| `services` entry | What it enables |
| --- | --- |
| `"fabric"` | Workspace and item discovery |
| `"sql"` | Warehouse, Lakehouse and SQL Database queries |
| `"onelake"` | OneLake files and tables |
| `"dax"` | Semantic model queries |
| `"kql"` | KQL queries |
| `"graphql"` | GraphQL queries |

For workspace discovery, use `services = "fabric"`. Then add this inside
`server()`, with a `verbatimTextOutput("workspaces")` in the UI:

```{r fabric-workspaces}
fabric <- oauth_db_fabric_api(auth$connection)

output$workspaces <- shiny::renderPrint({
  fabric$call(fabricQueryR::fabric_workspaces)
})
```

To query KQL, include `"kql"` in `services` and supply the function's normal
connection and query arguments:

```{r fabric-kql}
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  fabric$call(
    fabricQueryR::fabric_kql_query,
    cluster = "https://example.kusto.fabric.microsoft.com",
    database = "Events",
    query = "Events | take 20"
  )
})
```

The app registration needs the relevant delegated permissions, and the user
needs access to the workspace, item, and data. Enabling a service here
configures the OAuth request; it doesn't grant that access.

## Fabric resource objects

fabricQueryR returns workspace and item objects with methods for working with
them. You can use those methods with the same sign-in.

For example, configure `services = c("fabric", "onelake")`, then read a
Lakehouse table:

```{r fabric-lakehouse}
lakehouse <- shiny::reactive({
  fabric$call(
    fabricQueryR::fabric_item,
    workspace = "workspace-guid",
    item = "lakehouse-guid"
  )
})

output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  lakehouse()$read_table("Orders", limit = 100L)
})
```

These are fabricQueryR's R6 objects. A Warehouse offers `$sql_query(sql)`;
a semantic model offers `$dax_query(dax)`. Include `"sql"` or `"dax"` in
`services` for those methods. See fabricQueryR's help for its other methods
and arguments.

A resource object keeps the authorization used to create it. Recreate it
after changing the selected account; putting discovery in `reactive()`,
as above, does this for you.

## Databricks functions

Install `brickster` and use the Databricks sign-in client described in
[Database connections](databases.html). Inside `server()`:

```{r databricks-api}
databricks <- oauth_db_databricks_api(
  auth$connection,
  host = "example.cloud.databricks.com"
)

output$warehouses <- shiny::renderPrint({
  databricks$call(brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list)
})

output$rows <- shiny::renderPrint({
  databricks$call(
    brickster::db_sql_query,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id",
    statement = "SELECT current_user()",
    disposition = "INLINE",
    show_progress = FALSE
  )
})
```

Use `verbatimTextOutput()` for these outputs. The client supplies `host`
and a current token, so leave them out of the function's arguments. For Entra
authentication, use `auth_mode = "entra"` with a Microsoft client configured
for `services = "databricks_entra"`.

## Direct token callbacks

If you prefer to call a Fabric function directly, pass
`token = fabric$token_provider()`. For a single service, `oauth_db_fabric()`
also returns a function you can call to obtain a token callback; its help
page shows that alternative.

API clients don't close database connections opened by those functions
or resource methods. Use `oauth_db_fabric_sql()` or `oauth_db_databricks()`
for a connection managed by shinyOAuthDB.
